raw_response:
Aiyo, let me sit down and think about this year's planting. My old man will want to know what we're doing too.

---

**Thinking it through (in my own voice):**

My name doesn't matter much — I'm just an old farmer woman. I've worked these 7.5 mu for thirty years, since I married into this village. The land knows me and I know it. Every piece — which corner holds water after rain, which strip dries out first, where the soil is heavier — I don't need anyone to tell me.

We have eight mouths at home but most of the young ones aren't really at home. My two sons work in Shijiazhuang, my daughter-in-law too. They send money back but they come home only at spring festival and for wheat harvest if they can. So really it's me and my old man in the field. I'm 55, he's 58. We still do what we can.

**For the wheat** — I always plant around Cold Dew (寒露), maybe October 10 or so. That's what we've done every year. The seed I buy at the supply store in town, the common variety everyone plants — Jimai something, I don't remember the name, but it's the one the seed guy recommends because everyone in our village uses it. Maybe 30 jin per mu (about 15 kg). Cheap enough.

For fertilizer, before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's 50 jin, the 15-15-15 one. One bag costs around 170 yuan. Then when the wheat comes back up in spring, at jointing time (拔节), I topdress maybe 20 jin of urea per mu. That's what my neighbor Lao Wang does and his wheat always looks good. I used to put more but urea has gotten expensive, and last year with 20 jin it was still alright. If I see the wheat looking yellow I might add a little more, but usually 20 jin is enough.

Water — our well still works, thanks heaven. I water three times: once before winter so the roots don't freeze dry (冬水), once at jointing with the urea, and once when it's filling the grain. Last year we had good spring rain and I skipped one watering and saved some pumping money. It depends on the sky.

Pests — I spray the herbicide once in spring for the weeds, must do. If aphids come at the heading time I spray, otherwise I don't. I don't waste money spraying what isn't there.

For planting and harvest I hire the machine. We can't plant 7.5 mu by hand anymore, my back isn't what it was. The combine in June costs about 60 yuan per mu, worth it because my sons can't always come back to help.

**For the maize** — as soon as wheat comes off in June, we have to get maize in fast, within five or seven days. I buy hybrid seed fresh every year — you can't save it, my daughter-in-law tried once years ago and the yield was terrible. The seed guy has a variety most people buy, Zhengdan or whatever, about 40 yuan per mu of seed.

I direct-plant right into the wheat stubble, no plowing. Who has time to plow? The hired machine does it in one pass. I put one bag of compound fertilizer down with the seed — same as the wheat, 50 jin per mu. Later around the tasseling time (吐穗) I throw down 15-20 jin of urea if it looks like it needs it.

Maize doesn't need as much water if rain comes. Usually I water once after planting if it's dry, and maybe once at tasseling if it's a hot summer. Sometimes I don't water at all, depends on heaven.

I spray herbicide at planting — if you don't, the weeds take over and then it's a disaster. No insecticide usually. Harvest in late September with the machine again.

**Money matters** — seven and a half mu isn't much. After all the inputs and machine hire, we maybe clear a few thousand yuan for the year if prices are decent. Without my sons sending money, we couldn't live. That's why I don't waste money on extra fertilizer or spraying. Every bag I don't need to buy is real money saved.
